Mia (CSM): Heads-up — Paladin Health wants a short pilot in APAC (sg region) next Tue. They need an allowlist + temporary QPS bump for 4h window during demo. Can we do preprod peering + burst?
Raj (NetOps): Yep, we can provision peering and add allowlist for a CIDR. Need the exact IP ranges + desired qps and window.
Mia (CSM): Sending details from their infra lead in a sec. Window 2024-11-05 02:00–06:00 UTC, bump from 100 -> 200 qps. CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.45/32 (ephemeral).
Anya (Support): Noted. I'll create a support ticket and link the onboarding playbook. JIRA: CS-4821.
deploy-bot: Support ticket created: CS-4821 by Anya. Assigning to netops.
Raj (NetOps): Quick checklist: 1) confirm CIDRs ok 2) request peering in sg 3) update control-plane allowlist 4) set auto-revoke 5) monitor tail-latency during window.
Tess (Security): We need a signed data processing addendum for their APAC pilot (SOC2 req). Also confirm IP ownership for the ephemeral address and whether they use a NAT gateway.
Mia (CSM): They confirmed NAT + ephemeral but will reserve that /32 for demo. Legal is OK with DPA (OA-332).
Oliver (AE): Renewal touchpoint in 2 weeks — smoothing this pilot will be key. Can we add a low-friction rollback in case of errors? :thumbsup:
Raj (NetOps): Yes — we'll add an interim fallback to our fallback model in eu-west as a soft failover. Also we will enable burst caps and set qps-limit parameter on the route.
Raj (NetOps): Config I'll push: `route.allowlist = ["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.45/32"]; route.qps_limit=200; route.auto_revoke="2024-11-05T06:05:00Z"`
Anya (Support): Adding these details to CS-4821. I'll attach the sample curl test for Paladin to validate connectivity: ```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\\n  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45" \\\n  -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/query
```
Mia (CSM): Can netops also add tracing tags so we can correlate for renewal metrics? e.g., `x-customer:paladin`
Raj (NetOps): Yep — will add `x-customer` and `pilot-window` tags. We'll surface token-level cost/latency in Console for the demo.
Tess (Security): Before we flip peering, run a quick port-scan whitelist test and confirm there are no open admin ports. Share results in the ticket.
Raj (NetOps): Will run scans; ETA 4h. Posting result here once done.
deploy-bot: NetOps change queued: change-id chg-99217. Planned exec: 2024-11-05T01:30:00Z (rollback window 02:15).
Mia (CSM): One more ask from Paladin: can the allowlist be applied to both preprod and prod routes for faster cutover? We prefer preprod only for the pilot — prod later if the demo passes.
Oliver (AE): Keep prod off for now — we want measurable success before committing prod capacity (renewal leverage).
Anya (Support): Paladin reminded about billing visibility — setting a temporary tag so finance can produce usage preview.
Raj (NetOps): Done — added `billing_tag:paladin-pilot` to the route.
Mia (CSM): Thanks all. Please post verification when done and include a short checklist in CS-4821. I’ll loop the customer and schedule a 30-min runbook review on Monday. :calendar: 
Raj (NetOps): Verification complete. Peering established, allowlist applied to preprod route, burst enabled, auto-revoke set. Port-scan ok (no admin ports). Change chg-99217 closed.
Anya (Support): CS-4821 updated with verification, runbook, rollback steps, and renewal note. Marking as ready-for-demo.
Mia (CSM): Great job 🙏. Follow-up: capture customer's qualitative feedback during demo — add to renewal playbook.
Oliver (AE): I'll run renewal check-in after demo. If metrics look good we can propose a committed Dedicated trial.
Tess (Security): Uploaded DPA confirmation. All security gates cleared.
Mia (CSM): Closing thread — demo scheduled, ticket CS-4821 closed after validation.
